A great article on the topic of triggers

Really being triggered, not offended, is when something sets off symptoms of a mental illness. For someone recovering from anorexia, encountering a trigger (such as discussion of diets or fasting) may cause them to start obsessing over the weight, have intrusive thoughts about their body or food, and experience significant anxiety or depression. For someone with PTSD, encountering a trigger may cause flashbacks, or anxiety.

Mental illness isn't a thing you work through, and then you're done and ready to go on with life. It can be a life-long battle. You roll your rock up the hill and... just as you think it's up... just as you think everything is finally going to be okay and you can move on with your life, the rock comes tumbling back down and you're back to where you started.

Life goes on, even when you're crazy. It's important to learn to confront your triggers but you can't always do that all at once. You have to conserve your energy and be able to get through the process of living your life. You still need to get to work, even if you didn't sleep last night due to nightmares. You need to get your college paper done, even if you spent the last three hours reliving the worst times in your life.

So you pick your battles. Today, you will give your friend a hug, even though touch makes your skin crawl, but you won't watch that movie with the graphic rape scene. You can't afford a panic attack today; there's too much on your plate. Tomorrow, you might not be able to afford that hug, or you might be able to watch that movie. The crucial thing is that you try to move forward in the long run.

Some people try to run from their triggers forever. They try to hide from their triggers because they don't want to suffer. If given the power to do so, they'll try to rearrange the world to keep their pain at bay. And the left is trying to give them this power. Unscrupulous opportunists are taking notice of this, and are now using "triggers" as a justification to rearrange the world in their puritanical image. (Alcohol, drugs, loud noises, and shouting are extremely common triggers. Note that the left isn't rallying to eliminate those from college campuses.)

The weaponizing of triggers to shut down conversations and facilitate censorship is wrong, but I honestly think trigger warnings have their use. I don't think they are particularly more burdensome than warning for spoilers, and they help a subset of the population get through the day. It may help some people try to avoid getting help forever, but I'm not sure if that can be stopped. And I think that trigger warnings can help dull the impulse towards censorship. To quote the article I linked above

Trigger warnings fight those who would like to be our masters in another way as well. They are one of our strongest weapons against the proponents of censorship. The proponents say “We can’t let you air that opinion, it might offend people.” Trigger warnings say “I am explaining to you exactly how this might offend you, so if you continuing listening to me you have volunteered to hear whatever I have to say, on your own head be it, and let no one else purport to protect you from yourself.”

TL;DR: triggers are things that set of mental illness symptoms, mental illness isn't something you just get over, sometimes avoiding triggers is necessary, you can't avoid them forever, and you can't rearrange society around your mental illness, but trigger warnings really aren't so bad honestly.
